source_caption:
To capture the impossibly cute, hyperactive energy of Boo, Pixar didn’t rely on a professional child actor. Instead, they brought in Mary Gibbs, the two-year-old daughter of Pixar story artist Rob Gibbs. Because a toddler cannot be directed to stand inside a sound booth and read a script, the audio engineers simply followed her around the recording studio with a boom microphone while she played. They pieced together her genuine babbles, giggles, and tantrums to create one of the most purely authentic and beloved vocal performances in animation history.
⠀
Monsters, Inc. (2001), directed by Pete Docter, starring John Goodman, Billy Crystal, Mary Gibbs. Two top-scaring monsters face an unprecedented crisis when an unfazed human toddler accidentally breaches their factory, forcing them to question their terrifying industry and risk everything to return her home safely.

source_details.synopsis: Monsters, Inc. is a 2001 American animated fantasy comedy film directed by Pete Docter, and written by Andrew Stanton and Daniel Gerson. Produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures, the film stars the voices of John Goodman, Billy Crystal, Steve Buscemi, James Coburn, Jennifer Tilly, and Mary Gibbs. It centers on two monsters, the hairy James P. "Sulley" Sullivan (Goodman) and his one-eyed partner and best friend Mike Wazowski (Crystal), who are employed at the titular energy-producing factory Monsters, Inc., which generates power by scaring human children.
